_meta.purpose: Broker-level trading conditions that are NOT instrument specifications: account types, margin call and stop-out levels, higher-margin-requirement windows, and how trading volume is defined.
_meta.why_this_file_exists: Account conditions decide what happens when a trade goes wrong (stop-out level), what your costs look like (spread vs commission), and when the platform demands more margin (HMR). None of that is visible in a pip-value calculation, and all of it can end an account.
_meta.verification_policy: Every value marked "verified": true was read from the official Exness Help Center on verified_on. Values marked "verified": false are marked UNVERIFIED and must be confirmed in the Personal Area or the trading terminal. Broker conditions are region- and account-specific: minimum initial deposit is explicitly region based in the official documentation, so no single figure is valid for everyone.
sources: https://get.exness.help/hc/en-us/articles/4408633634322-How-to-create-trading-accounts (account creation steps, demo availability, unchangeable account type/server)
https://get.exness.help/hc/en-us/articles/360014693340-Margin-call-and-stop-out-levels-by-account-type (margin call / stop out by account type)
https://get.exness.help/hc/en-us/articles/8633865683612-Why-is-the-margin-required-so-high-for-my-order (higher margin requirements before weekends and news)
https://get.exness.help/hc/en-us/articles/9662707664156-Trading-volume-calculation (trading volume = lots x contract size, in base currency)
https://get.exness.help/hc/en-us/articles/18043874767772-Trading-calculator (broker calculator: margin, spread cost, commission, swaps, pip value)
_meta.important_warning: These conditions change. Re-read the official sources before every new phase of trading, and treat anything in this file as a dated snapshot rather than a current guarantee.
_meta.not_advice: This file records documented broker conditions. It is not a recommendation to open, fund or trade any account.

environment_note: The project's programme requires a long demo phase before any live capital. 250 USD is the eventual live figure, and only after the readiness criteria pass.

account_types.name: Standard Cent
account_types.notes: Documented account suffix is -c. Demo accounts are NOT available for Standard Cent, so you cannot rehearse the exact cent-lot maths in a demo first. Cent lots are why this account matters on a very small live balance: 0.01 cent-lots are roughly 1/100th the money value of 0.01 standard lots, which is the honest workaround for the minimum-lot problem.

account_types.name: Standard
account_types.notes: Documented instruments: forex, metals, cryptocurrencies, commodities (metals and energies), stocks, indices. Cost is inside the spread. Documented maximum volume 200 lots during 07:00-20:59 GMT and 60 lots during 21:00-06:59 GMT.

account_types.name: Pro
account_types.notes: Execution type is chosen only for Pro accounts at creation. Higher margin call level (30%) than Standard: the warning arrives later, which is not a benefit.

account_types.name: Raw Spread
account_types.commission: up to 3.50 USD each side per lot
account_types.notes: Cost is split: near-zero spread plus commission. On 0.01 lots the commission is about 0.07 USD round turn. Cost per trade must be computed, not assumed: a tighter spread is not automatically cheaper at very small size.

account_types.name: Zero
account_types.commission: from 0.02 USD each side per lot
account_types.notes: Lowest documented commission per side. Still has costs, and still has a minimum lot.

stop_out_exceptions.stocks_under_market_risk: For stocks, the stop-out level may rise to 100% under increased market risk.
stop_out_exceptions.entity_specific: A stop out of 20% applies for clients registered via Exness (KE) Limited and Exness Limited Jordan Ltd.
stop_out_exceptions.consequence: Never assume the documented 0% applies to your account. Confirm the margin call and stop-out levels for YOUR entity and account type before trading, because the difference between 0% and 20% decides whether a single position can empty the account.

zero_stop_out_explanation: A 0% stop out means positions may only be closed when the margin level reaches 0%, i.e. when equity is essentially exhausted. It is not a protective feature for the trader: it shifts the responsibility for stopping out onto your own stop loss and your own size decision.

higher_margin_requirements.summary: Exness documents that margin requirements increase before volatile events, in periods it calls Higher Margin Requirements (HMR).

weekend_window.quote: For most instruments, from 3 hours before a weekend close until 1 hour after the market reopens, margin is calculated using the instrument's maximum leverage.
weekend_window.crypto_exception: Cryptocurrencies trade 24/7, so weekend HMR does not apply to them.
weekend_window.interpretation: Interpretation, not a quote: margin can be several times larger than usual in this window, so a position that fits comfortably on Friday morning may not fit on Friday evening. For a small account the practical rule is simpler: do not carry positions through the weekend while learning.

news_window.quote: For most instruments, positions opened 15 minutes before a news release until 90 seconds after are limited to the instrument's maximum leverage during HMR.
news_window.existing_positions: Existing positions remain unaffected, except for stocks, where previously opened orders may also be recalculated during financial report announcements.
news_window.interpretation: Interpretation: the leverage used for margin is capped during this window, which can raise the margin a new order needs at exactly the moment spreads widen. The system's news blackout (no entry 30 minutes before / 15 minutes after) keeps you out of the window entirely.

higher_margin_requirements.duration_caveat: The HMR period depends on the instrument and the event, and may last longer based on risk management decisions.
higher_margin_requirements.how_to_know: An HMR banner appears on charts in the Exness Terminal and Exness Trade, and the New Order window always shows the leverage that will be used for margin calculation.

trading_volume.definition: Trading volume is always calculated in the base currency.
trading_volume.formula: TV = number of lots x contract size
trading_volume.why_it_matters: TV is what margin and pip value are derived from. It is not the same as your risk: TV describes the size of the position, risk describes the distance to invalidation priced in money.

broker_calculator.where: Personal Area > Tools & Services, and in the Exness Trade app.
documented_caveats: Spread cost is based on the average spread of the previous trading day; the actual spread cost can only be determined when a real order is opened.
Results depend on the account type, account currency, instrument, volume and leverage.
For instruments with fixed margin requirements, the leverage setting is disabled.
broker_calculator.comparison_with_this_project: The broker calculator is the authority on that broker's own conditions and should be used to sanity-check results. This project's engine differs on purpose in two ways: it refuses to run at all when a conversion rate is unknown (MissingRateError) instead of assuming a rate, and it reports the minimum-lot problem as a hard error instead of silently rounding a size up. Use both, and treat any disagreement as a finding to investigate.

risk_rules_for_this_project.source: config/strategy_rules.json and config/risk_profile.json - these are this project's rules, not broker rules.
